indicator.subject: Mathematics
indicator.content_standard: B5.3.1.1 Identify and sort quadrilaterals, including rectangles, squares, trapezoids, parallelograms, and rhombuses, according to their attributes
indicator.objective: Demonstrate an understanding of the properties (e.g. sides, angles, and diagonals) of squares and rectangles

skills.description: Identify properties of a square (4 equal sides, 4 right angles, equal diagonals bisecting at 90°).
Identify properties of a rectangle (opposite sides equal, 4 right angles, equal diagonals bisecting at non-90°).

spec.difficultyPlan: 20 questions: 5 at difficulty 1, 7 at difficulty 2, 5 at difficulty 3, 3 at difficulty 4.
misconceptions: Thinking a square is not a rectangle.
Thinking all rectangles have equal diagonals that bisect at right angles.

questions.stem: How many equal sides does a square have?
hints: All sides of a square are the same length.

questions.stem: What type of angles does a square have?
hints: Each corner is a square corner.
questions.misconception: Saying acute angles because they look sharp.

questions.stem: How many pairs of equal opposite sides does a rectangle have?
hints: Top and bottom are equal, left and right are equal.
questions.explanation: A rectangle has 2 pairs of equal opposite sides.
questions.misconception: Saying 4 pairs because it has 4 sides.

questions.stem: What type of angles does a rectangle have?
hints: Each corner is a square corner.

options: A square is a special type of rectangle.
A rectangle is a special type of square.
A square and a rectangle are not related.
hints: A square has all the properties of a rectangle.
questions.explanation: A square is a special rectangle with all sides equal.

questions.stem: A square has sides of 5 cm. What is the length of each diagonal? (Hint: Diagonal = side × √2, but for a square with side 5, use 5√2 ≈ 7.07 cm. Round to nearest whole number.)
A rectangle has length 8 cm and width 6 cm. What is the length of its diagonal?
Which of these is NOT a property of a square?
hints: Diagonals of a square bisect at 90°.
questions.explanation: Diagonals of a square bisect at 90°, not 60°.
questions.misconception: Thinking diagonals bisect at any angle.

questions.stem: Which of these is true about the diagonals of a rectangle?
hints: In a rectangle, diagonals are equal.
questions.explanation: The diagonals of a rectangle are equal in length.

questions.stem: Explain why a square can be called a rectangle.
hints: Check the properties of a rectangle.
questions.explanation: A square has 4 right angles and opposite sides equal, which are the defining properties of a rectangle.
questions.misconception: Thinking squares and rectangles are mutually exclusive.

questions.stem: How many lines of symmetry does a square have?
hints: Two diagonals, one vertical, one horizontal.
questions.explanation: A square has 4 lines of symmetry.

questions.stem: How many lines of symmetry does a rectangle have?
questions.explanation: A rectangle has 2 lines of symmetry.

questions.stem: Explain how the diagonals of a square are related.
hints: They are equal, bisect each other, and meet at 90°.
questions.explanation: The diagonals of a square are equal in length, bisect each other, and intersect at right angles.

criteria.description: States they bisect at right angles.

questions.stem: A rectangle has diagonals of length 13 cm. If the length is 12 cm, what is the width?
Which property is true for a square but NOT always true for a rectangle?
hints: A rectangle may have unequal sides.
questions.explanation: A square has all sides equal, but a rectangle does not necessarily.
questions.misconception: Thinking all rectangles have equal sides.

questions.stem: Explain the difference between the diagonals of a square and a rectangle in terms of how they intersect.
hints: Think about the angle at which they cross.
questions.explanation: The diagonals of a square intersect at 90° (perpendicular), while the diagonals of a rectangle do not necessarily intersect at 90°.

criteria.description: States rectangle diagonals do not necessarily meet at 90°.

questions.misconception: Thinking all rectangles have perpendicular diagonals.

questions.stem: A square has side length s. What is the length of its diagonal?
A rectangle has length L and width W. Write an expression for the length of its diagonal.
A pupil says 'All squares are rectangles, but not all rectangles are squares.' Explain why this is true.
questions.explanation: A square meets all the criteria for a rectangle (4 right angles, opposite sides equal). However, a rectangle may have unequal sides, so it may not be a square.

criteria.description: States rectangle may have unequal sides.
